text: Eight thousand kilometres away, in Europe, the evening sky turns blood red.
High above the clouds, sulphur gas from the volcano would spread into a thin veil around the planet, reflecting sunlight back into space.
The whole Earth could cool by a few degrees.
In 1815, a far smaller eruption, Tambora, caused the year without a summer.
Harvests failed across Europe, and food prices soared.
A supereruption could be many times worse.
The chance of it happening in any given year is tiny, about one in seven hundred thousand.
But somewhere on Earth, it has happened before… and it will happen again.
So if it happened tomorrow… how far away would you want to be?
